claim: 72% of cancer-associated ATM mutations are missense mutations
source: Here we report that 72% of cancer-associated ATM mutations are missense mutations that are enriched around the kinase domain.
evidence: Based on analysis of 286 unique non-synonymous mutations from TCGA database as shown in Figure 1A

claim: Cancer-associated ATM missense mutations are enriched around the kinase domain
source: Here we report that 72% of cancer-associated ATM mutations are missense mutations that are enriched around the kinase domain.
evidence: Supported by mutation density analyses and permutation analyses showing 2.5 fold enrichment in kinase domain (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A)

claim: Expression of kinase-dead ATM (AtmKD/-) is more oncogenic than loss of ATM (Atm-/-) in mouse models
source: Expression of kinase-dead ATM (AtmKD/-) is more oncogenic than loss of ATM (Atm-/-) in mouse models, leading to earlier and more frequent lymphomas with Pten deletions.
evidence: Demonstrated by survival curves showing 35 days shorter median survival and 34% increased lifetime risk in VKD vs VN mice (Figure 2D-E)

claim: AtmKD/- mice develop earlier lymphomas than Atm-/- mice
source: Expression of kinase-dead ATM (AtmKD/-) is more oncogenic than loss of ATM (Atm-/-) in mouse models, leading to earlier and more frequent lymphomas with Pten deletions.
evidence: Median survival of thymic lymphoma bearing VKD mice is ~35 days shorter than VN mice (104 vs 139 days, p=0.03) as shown in Figure 2E

claim: AtmKD/- mice develop more frequent lymphomas than Atm-/- mice
source: Expression of kinase-dead ATM (AtmKD/-) is more oncogenic than loss of ATM (Atm-/-) in mouse models, leading to earlier and more frequent lymphomas with Pten deletions.
evidence: 75% of VKD mice succumbed to lymphomas representing a 34% increase over the 56% life-time risk among VN mice (Figure 2D)

claim: AtmKD/- lymphomas have Pten deletions
source: Expression of kinase-dead ATM (AtmKD/-) is more oncogenic than loss of ATM (Atm-/-) in mouse models, leading to earlier and more frequent lymphomas with Pten deletions.
evidence: CGH and immunoblotting showed all VKD thymic lymphomas carried deep deletions at the Pten locus while none of the VN controls did (Figure 2F-G)

claim: Kinase-dead ATM protein prevents replication-dependent removal of Topo-isomerase I-DNA adducts at the step of strand cleavage
source: Kinase-dead ATM protein (Atm-KD), but not loss of ATM (Atm-null), prevents replication-dependent removal of Topo-isomerase I-DNA adducts at the step of strand cleavage, leading to severe genomic instability and hypersensitivity to Topo-isomerase I inhibitors.
evidence: Demonstrated by accumulation of Top1cc in AtmKD/- cells (Figure 5A), reduced CPT-induced DSBs (Figure 6C-E), and reduced SCEs (Figure 5D)

claim: Loss of ATM does not prevent replication-dependent removal of Topo-isomerase I-DNA adducts
source: Kinase-dead ATM protein (Atm-KD), but not loss of ATM (Atm-null), prevents replication-dependent removal of Topo-isomerase I-DNA adducts at the step of strand cleavage, leading to severe genomic instability and hypersensitivity to Topo-isomerase I inhibitors.
evidence: Atm-/- cells show normal CPT-induced SCEs (Figure 5D) and less Top1cc accumulation than AtmKD/- cells (Figure 5A)

claim: Topo-isomerase I inhibitors effectively and preferentially eliminate AtmKD/- leukemia in animal models
source: Correspondingly, Topo-isomerase I inhibitors effectively and preferentially eliminate AtmKD/-, but not Atm-proficientor Atm-/- leukemia in animal models.
evidence: Irinotecan treatment eradicated AtmKD/- leukemia but not AtmKD/C or Atm-/- leukemia as shown by reduced GFP+ cells, spleen size, and increased apoptosis (Figure 4B-F)

claim: Topo-isomerase I inhibitors do not effectively eliminate Atm-proficient leukemia in animal models
source: Correspondingly, Topo-isomerase I inhibitors effectively and preferentially eliminate AtmKD/-, but not Atm-proficientor Atm-/- leukemia in animal models.
evidence: Irinotecan had no significant benefit in AtmC/C leukemia (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C-F, p≥0.05)

claim: Topo-isomerase I inhibitors do not effectively eliminate Atm-/- leukemia in animal models
source: Correspondingly, Topo-isomerase I inhibitors effectively and preferentially eliminate AtmKD/-, but not Atm-proficientor Atm-/- leukemia in animal models.
evidence: Irinotecan had no significant benefit in Atm-/- leukemia (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C-F, p≥0.05)

claim: Among 5402 cases in TCGA, 286 unique non-synonymous mutations of ATM were identified
source: Among the 5402 cases in The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), we identified 286 unique non-synonymous mutations of ATM.
evidence: Direct statement of data analysis results from TCGA database

claim: Truncating mutations compose 83% of A-T associated point mutations
source: While truncating (nonsense/frameshift) mutations compose 83% (373/447) of A-T associated point mutations (>1000 patients), 72% (206/286) of non-synonymous point mutations of ATM in TCGA are missense mutations (Figure 1A, Supplementary file 1A,B).
evidence: Based on analysis of >1000 A-T patients from Leiden open variable database as shown in Figure 1A

claim: The ATM gene is not hyper-mutated in TCGA
source: Permutation analyses show that ATM gene is not hyper-mutated, but the kinase-domain is mutated 2.5 fold more frequently than otherwise expected in TCGA (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, p<0.01).
evidence: Permutation analyses comparing actual vs expected mutation frequencies (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A)

claim: The ATM kinase-domain is mutated 2.5 fold more frequently than otherwise expected in TCGA
source: Permutation analyses show that ATM gene is not hyper-mutated, but the kinase-domain is mutated 2.5 fold more frequently than otherwise expected in TCGA (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, p<0.01).
evidence: Permutation analyses showing statistically significant enrichment (p<0.01) in kinase domain (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A)

claim: Cancer associated missense ATM mutations in TCGA cluster around the C-terminal kinase domain
source: The mutation density calculated using the Gaussian Kernel model revealed that cancer associated missense ATM mutations in TCGA cluster around the C-terminal kinase domain, while truncating mutations (in A-T or TCGA) span the entire ATM protein (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Gaussian Kernel density analysis showing clustering pattern (Figure 1B)

claim: Truncating ATM mutations span the entire ATM protein
source: The mutation density calculated using the Gaussian Kernel model revealed that cancer associated missense ATM mutations in TCGA cluster around the C-terminal kinase domain, while truncating mutations (in A-T or TCGA) span the entire ATM protein (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Gaussian Kernel density analysis showing distribution pattern (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B)

claim: The kinase and FATC domains of ATM share 31% sequence identity with mTOR
source: The kinase and FATC domains of ATM share 31% sequence identity with mTOR, a related phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase-related protein kinase (PIKK) for which the high resolution crystal structure is available (Yang et al., 2013).
evidence: Based on sequence comparison between ATM and mTOR used for homology modeling

claim: 64% of ATM kinase domain missense mutations from TCGA affect highly conserved residues
source: Homology modeling using mTOR (PDB 4JSP) (Yang et al., 2013) revealed that 64% (27/42) (at 18 unique amino acids) of ATM kinase domain missense mutations from TCGA, affect highly conserved residues and 50% (21/42) of the mutations (red on the ribbon structure) likely abolish kinase activity based on structural analyses (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Homology modeling analysis using mTOR crystal structure (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C)

claim: 50% of ATM kinase domain missense mutations from TCGA likely abolish kinase activity
source: Homology modeling using mTOR (PDB 4JSP) (Yang et al., 2013) revealed that 64% (27/42) (at 18 unique amino acids) of ATM kinase domain missense mutations from TCGA, affect highly conserved residues and 50% (21/42) of the mutations (red on the ribbon structure) likely abolish kinase activity based on structural analyses (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Structural analysis based on homology modeling (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C)

claim: Residues K2717, D2720, H2872, D2870, N2875 and D2889 of human ATM are predicted to bind ATP or the essential Mg+ ion
source: Specifically, residues K2717, D2720, H2872, D2870, N2875 and D2889 of human ATM are predicted to bind ATP or the essential Mg+ ion (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Structural prediction based on homology modeling with mTOR (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D)

claim: N2875 is mutated in two TCGA cases at the time of initial analyses
source: Notably, N2875 is mutated in two TCGA cases at the time of initial analyses.
evidence: Direct observation from TCGA database analysis

claim: One of the two N2875 mutation cases has concurrent shallow deletion in the ATM region
source: One of the two cases have concurrent shallow deletion in this region (Supplementary file 1B).
evidence: Data from TCGA analysis (Supplementary file 1B)

claim: An additional N2875 mutation was reported in a prostate cancer case with an allele frequency of 0.92
source: Since then, one additional N2875 mutation was reported in a prostate cancer case (TCGA-YL-A8S9) with an allele frequency of 0.92, consistent with homozygosity.
evidence: Data from TCGA database for case TCGA-YL-A8S9

claim: The N2875K and D2870A combination abolishes ATM kinase activity without significantly affecting ATM protein levels
source: Mutations corresponding to N2875K of human ATM were previously engineered into the AtmKD/+ mice together with the corresponding D2870A mutation of human ATM. This combination was found to abolish ATM kinase activity without significantly affecting ATM protein levels (Yamamoto et al., 2012; Canman, 1998).
evidence: Previous experimental findings in mouse models

claim: Several human cancer cell lines with missense mutations around the kinase domain express catalytically inactive ATM protein
source: Finally, immunoblotting confirmed the expression of catalytically inactive ATM protein in several human cancer cell lines with missense mutations around the kinase domain (CCLE, Broad Institute) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E–F).
evidence: Western blot analysis showing ATM expression but lack of pKap1 after IR (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E-F)

claim: VavCre efficiently inactivates the Atm conditional allele in all blood cells including lymphocytes
source: In these mice, the HSC-specific Cre recombinase (VavCre) (de Boer et al., 2003) efficiently inactivates the Atm conditional (AtmC) allele (Zha et al., 2008; Callén et al., 2009) in all blood cells including lymphocytes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Southern blot showing complete deletion in lymphoid lineage (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A)

claim: VKD and VN mice display defects in B cell CSR similar to Atm-/- mice
source: VKD and VN mice display defects in B cell CSR and T cell development similar to Atm-/- mice, namely 50% decrease of CSR (to IgG1), reduced expression of surface-TCRβ/CD3 in CD4+CD8+ double-positive (DP) cells, and partial blockage at DP to CD4+CD8- or CD4-CD8+ single-positive (SP) T cell transitions (Borghesani et al., 2000; Lumsden et al., 2004; Reina-San-Martin et al., 2004) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B–C), supporting efficient inactivation of AtmC allele in VKD and VN lymphocytes.
evidence: FACS and CSR assays showing similar defects (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B-C)

claim: VKD and VN mice show 50% decrease of CSR to IgG1
source: VKD and VN mice display defects in B cell CSR and T cell development similar to Atm-/- mice, namely 50% decrease of CSR (to IgG1), reduced expression of surface-TCRβ/CD3 in CD4+CD8+ double-positive (DP) cells, and partial blockage at DP to CD4+CD8- or CD4-CD8+ single-positive (SP) T cell transitions (Borghesani et al., 2000; Lumsden et al., 2004; Reina-San-Martin et al., 2004) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B–C), supporting efficient inactivation of AtmC allele in VKD and VN lymphocytes.
evidence: CSR assay results (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B-C)

claim: VKD thymocytes are partially blocked at the DN3 stage
source: Immature T cells with productive TCRβ rearrangements undergo rapid proliferation and expansion in the CD4-CD8- double-negative (DN) 3 stage (CD44-CD25+). VKD thymocytes, but not VN or Atm-/- thymocytes, are partially blocked at the DN3 stage, consistent with proliferation defects in AtmKD/- cell (Yamamoto et al., 2012) (Figure 2A–B).
evidence: FACS analysis showing increased DN3 percentage in VKD mice (Figure 2A-B)

claim: VN and Atm-/- thymocytes are not blocked at the DN3 stage
source: Immature T cells with productive TCRβ rearrangements undergo rapid proliferation and expansion in the CD4-CD8- double-negative (DN) 3 stage (CD44-CD25+). VKD thymocytes, but not VN or Atm-/- thymocytes, are partially blocked at the DN3 stage, consistent with proliferation defects in AtmKD/- cell (Yamamoto et al., 2012) (Figure 2A–B).
evidence: FACS analysis showing normal DN3 progression (Figure 2A-B)

claim: Thymocyte number in VKD mice was reduced ~60% compared to VN littermates
source: As a result, thymocyte number in VKD mice was reduced ~60% compared to their VN littermates (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Quantification of total thymocyte counts (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C)

claim: About 8% of VKD mice developed clonal pro-B cell lymphomas
source: About 8% of the VKD, but none of the VN mice, also developed clonal pro-B cell lymphomas (B220+CD43+IgM-) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B–C).
evidence: FACS and Southern blot analyses (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B-C)

claim: None of the VN mice developed clonal pro-B cell lymphomas
source: About 8% of the VKD, but none of the VN mice, also developed clonal pro-B cell lymphomas (B220+CD43+IgM-) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B–C).
evidence: FACS and Southern blot analyses showing absence of B-cell lymphomas in VN mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B-C)

claim: All VKD thymic lymphomas carried deep deletions at the Pten locus
source: Comparative genome hybridization (CGH) showed that all VKD thymic lymphomas, but none of the VN controls, carried deep deletions at the Pten locus (Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: CGH analysis results (Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A)

claim: None of the VN thymic lymphomas carried deep deletions at the Pten locus
source: Comparative genome hybridization (CGH) showed that all VKD thymic lymphomas, but none of the VN controls, carried deep deletions at the Pten locus (Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: CGH analysis results (Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A)

claim: All but one VKD tumors showed severe reductions of Pten protein levels
source: Immunoblotting of additional lymphomas revealed severe reductions of Pten protein levels in all but one of the VKD tumors, while most VN tumors retained Pten expression.
evidence: Western blot analysis of Pten protein (Figure 2G)

claim: Most VN tumors retained Pten expression
source: Immunoblotting of additional lymphomas revealed severe reductions of Pten protein levels in all but one of the VKD tumors, while most VN tumors retained Pten expression.
evidence: Western blot analysis of Pten protein (Figure 2G)

claim: The only Pten-expressing VKD tumor appeared to have lost Atm-KD expression
source: The only Pten-expressing VKD tumor (6684) appeared to have lost Atm-KD expression (Figure 2G).
evidence: Western blot showing absence of ATM protein in tumor 6684 (Figure 2G)

claim: Pten deletion was previously found in ~25% of germline Atm-/- or Tp53-/- thymic lymphomas
source: Pten deletion was previously found in ~25% of germline Atm-/- or Tp53-/- thymic lymphomas and was thought to occur in the early progenitors before T cell commitment (Zha et al., 2010; Dudgeon et al., 2014).
evidence: Previous published findings

claim: Frequency of chromatid breaks are significantly higher in VKD T cells than in VN or Atm+/+ T cells
source: Consistent with this model, frequency of chromatid breaks are significantly higher in VKD T cells, than in VN or Atm+/+ T cells (Figure 2H).
evidence: Telomere FISH analyses of metaphase spreads (Figure 2H)

claim: AtmKD/- and Atm-/- MEFs were similarly sensitive to ionizing radiation
source: While both AtmKD/- and Atm-/- MEFs were similarly sensitive to ionizing radiation (IR), AtmKD/- cells were significantly more sensitive to the Topo1 inhibitor camptothecin (CPT) than Atm-/- and Atm+/- cells (Figure 3A–B).
evidence: Cell survival assays showing similar IR sensitivity (Figure 3A)

claim: AtmKD/- cells were significantly more sensitive to camptothecin than Atm-/- and Atm+/- cells
source: While both AtmKD/- and Atm-/- MEFs were similarly sensitive to ionizing radiation (IR), AtmKD/- cells were significantly more sensitive to the Topo1 inhibitor camptothecin (CPT) than Atm-/- and Atm+/- cells (Figure 3A–B).
evidence: Cell survival assays showing differential CPT sensitivity (Figure 3B, p<0.001)

claim: AtmKD/- cells were not hypersensitive to etoposide
source: The CPT hypersensitivity of AtmKD/- cells does not appear to reflect an inability to process blocked DNA ends or overcome replication blockage in general, as AtmKD/- cells were not hypersensitive to etoposide, a Topoisomerase II inhibitor, nor to two replication blocking agents, hydroxyurea (HU) or aphidicolin (APH), (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Cell survival assays showing similar etoposide sensitivity (Figure 3C)

claim: AtmKD/- cells were not hypersensitive to hydroxyurea
source: The CPT hypersensitivity of AtmKD/- cells does not appear to reflect an inability to process blocked DNA ends or overcome replication blockage in general, as AtmKD/- cells were not hypersensitive to etoposide, a Topoisomerase II inhibitor, nor to two replication blocking agents, hydroxyurea (HU) or aphidicolin (APH), (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Cell survival assays (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B)

claim: AtmKD/- cells were not hypersensitive to aphidicolin
source: The CPT hypersensitivity of AtmKD/- cells does not appear to reflect an inability to process blocked DNA ends or overcome replication blockage in general, as AtmKD/- cells were not hypersensitive to etoposide, a Topoisomerase II inhibitor, nor to two replication blocking agents, hydroxyurea (HU) or aphidicolin (APH), (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Cell survival assays (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B)

claim: AtmKD/- primary T cells are hypersensitive to CPT compared to corresponding ATM+/+ or Atm-/- controls
source: Moreover, AtmKD/- primary T cells and the human cancer cell lines that express ATM-KD protein identified in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F are also hypersensitive to CPT compared to corresponding ATM+/+ or Atm-/- controls (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Cell survival assays on primary T cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E)

claim: Human cancer cell lines that express ATM-KD protein are hypersensitive to CPT compared to corresponding ATM+/+ controls
source: Moreover, AtmKD/- primary T cells and the human cancer cell lines that express ATM-KD protein identified in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F are also hypersensitive to CPT compared to corresponding ATM+/+ or Atm-/- controls (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Cell survival assays on human cancer cell lines (Figure 3D, p<0.0001)

claim: shRNA knockdown of mutated ATM in Granta519 moderately rescued the CPT hypersensitivity
source: Finally, shRNA knockdown of mutated ATM in Granta519 human lymphomas cell lines, moderately, yet significantly, rescued the CPT hypersensitivity and CPT induced apoptosis associated with the expression of catalytically inactive ATM (Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: shRNA knockdown experiments showing rescue of CPT sensitivity (Figure 3E, p=7.28x10E-6)

claim: shRNA knockdown of mutated ATM in Granta519 significantly rescued CPT induced apoptosis
source: Finally, shRNA knockdown of mutated ATM in Granta519 human lymphomas cell lines, moderately, yet significantly, rescued the CPT hypersensitivity and CPT induced apoptosis associated with the expression of catalytically inactive ATM (Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: Apoptosis assays showing reduced apoptosis after ATM knockdown (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C-D)

claim: AtmKD/- MEFs accumulated Top1cc even at low CPT concentrations (0.1 µM)
source: We found that AtmKD/-, but not Atm-/- or Atm+/+ MEFs accumulated Top1cc even at low CPT concentrations (0.1 µM) (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: ICE assay results (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and B)

claim: Atm-/- MEFs do not accumulate Top1cc at low CPT concentrations (0.1 µM)
source: We found that AtmKD/-, but not Atm-/- or Atm+/+ MEFs accumulated Top1cc even at low CPT concentrations (0.1 µM) (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: ICE assay results (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and B)

claim: ATM kinase inhibitor leads to CPT-dependent Top1cc-accumulation in Atm+/- MEFs
source: ATM kinase inhibitor (ATMi, KU55933, 15 µM) also leads to CPT-dependent Top1cc-accumulation in Atm+/- MEFs (Figure 5A).
evidence: ICE assay with ATM inhibitor treatment (Figure 5A)

claim: At high CPT concentration (15 µM), the Top1cc level is greatest in AtmKD/- cells, followed by Atm-/-, then Atm+/+
source: At high CPT concentration (15 µM), the Top1cc level is greatest in AtmKD/- cells, followed by Atm-/-, then Atm+/+(Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: ICE assay results at high CPT concentration (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and B)

claim: CPT-induced degradation of full-length Topo1 is not significantly affected in AtmKD/- or Atm-/- MEFs
source: Meanwhile, CPT-induced degradation of full-length Topo1, necessary for its subsequent removal (Pommier, 2006), is not significantly affected in AtmKD/- or Atm-/- MEFs (Figure 5B).
evidence: Western blot analysis of Topo1 protein levels (Figure 5B)

claim: CPT-induced SCEs were reduced in AtmKD/- MEFs
source: CPT (1 µM) induced SCEs were reduced in AtmKD/- MEFs, but not Atm-/- MEFs, and ATM inhibitor decreased CPT-induced SCEs in Atm+/-, but not in Atm-/- MEFs (Figure 5D), suggesting a defect at replication-dependent removal of Top1cc in the AtmKD/- cells.
evidence: SCE assay results (Figure 5D, p=0.007 and p=0.001)

claim: CPT-induced SCEs were not reduced in Atm-/- MEFs
source: CPT (1 µM) induced SCEs were reduced in AtmKD/- MEFs, but not Atm-/- MEFs, and ATM inhibitor decreased CPT-induced SCEs in Atm+/-, but not in Atm-/- MEFs (Figure 5D), suggesting a defect at replication-dependent removal of Top1cc in the AtmKD/- cells.
evidence: SCE assay results (Figure 5D)

claim: ATM inhibitor decreased CPT-induced SCEs in Atm+/- MEFs
source: CPT (1 µM) induced SCEs were reduced in AtmKD/- MEFs, but not Atm-/- MEFs, and ATM inhibitor decreased CPT-induced SCEs in Atm+/-, but not in Atm-/- MEFs (Figure 5D), suggesting a defect at replication-dependent removal of Top1cc in the AtmKD/- cells.
evidence: SCE assay with ATM inhibitor (Figure 5D, p=0.007)

claim: ATM inhibitor did not decrease CPT-induced SCEs in Atm-/- MEFs
source: CPT (1 µM) induced SCEs were reduced in AtmKD/- MEFs, but not Atm-/- MEFs, and ATM inhibitor decreased CPT-induced SCEs in Atm+/-, but not in Atm-/- MEFs (Figure 5D), suggesting a defect at replication-dependent removal of Top1cc in the AtmKD/- cells.
evidence: SCE assay with ATM inhibitor in Atm-/- cells (Figure 5D, p=0.87)

claim: ATM kinase inhibitor did not suppress SCEs in Blm-/- MEFs
source: ATM kinase inhibitor did not suppress SCEs in Blmhelicase-deficient (Blm-/-) MEFs, suggesting that the lack of SCEs could not be simply explained by the bias in CO-generating holiday junction resolvases (e.g. MUS81, SLX1/4, GEN1) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C) (Chan and West, 2014).
evidence: SCE assay in Blm-/- cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C)

claim: HR is reduced by 50% in AtmKD/- embryonic stem cells
source: In this context, an integrated (at the Pim1 locus) DR-GFP reporter (Moynahan et al., 1999) revealed a 50% reduction of HR in AtmKD/- embryonic stem (ES) cells, but not in Atm-/- cells.
evidence: DR-GFP reporter assay results (Figure 5E, p<0.0001)

claim: HR is not reduced in Atm-/- embryonic stem cells
source: In this context, an integrated (at the Pim1 locus) DR-GFP reporter (Moynahan et al., 1999) revealed a 50% reduction of HR in AtmKD/- embryonic stem (ES) cells, but not in Atm-/- cells.
evidence: DR-GFP reporter assay results (Figure 5E)

claim: ATM inhibitor reduced HR in Atm+/+ ES cells
source: ATM inhibitor reduced HR in Atm+/+, but not Atm-/- ES cells (Figure 4D) (Rass et al., 2013; Kass et al., 2013), consistent with potential HR defects.
evidence: DR-GFP reporter assay with ATM inhibitor (Figure 5E, p<0.0001)

claim: ATM inhibitor did not reduce HR in Atm-/- ES cells
source: ATM inhibitor reduced HR in Atm+/+, but not Atm-/- ES cells (Figure 4D) (Rass et al., 2013; Kass et al., 2013), consistent with potential HR defects.
evidence: DR-GFP reporter assay with ATM inhibitor in Atm-/- cells (Figure 5E)

claim: IR induced phosphorylated-RPA (T21) foci were not significantly compromised in AtmKD/- cells
source: Yet IR induced phosphorylated-RPA (T21) and Rad51 foci, were not significantly compromised in AtmKD/- cells (Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A) (Shakya et al., 2011).
evidence: Immunofluorescence analysis of pRPA foci (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A)

claim: IR induced Rad51 foci were not significantly compromised in AtmKD/- cells
source: Yet IR induced phosphorylated-RPA (T21) and Rad51 foci, were not significantly compromised in AtmKD/- cells (Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A) (Shakya et al., 2011).
evidence: Immunofluorescence analysis of Rad51 foci after IR (Figure 6A, p=0.12)

claim: CPT-induced Rad51 foci were markedly decreased in AtmKD/- MEFs
source: In this regard, we found that CPT-induced Rad51 foci were markedly decreased in AtmKD/- MEFs (Figure 6B).
evidence: Immunofluorescence analysis of Rad51 foci after CPT treatment (Figure 6B, p=0.0022)

claim: CPT-induced DSBs measured by γ-H2AX were attenuated in AtmKD/- cells
source: Moreover CPT-induced DSBs measured by phosphorylated H2AX (γ-H2AX) and the neutral comet assay were also attenuated in AtmKD/- cells (but not Atm-/- cells) and by ATM kinase inhibitor (Figure 6C–E).
evidence: γ-H2AX foci quantification (Figure 6C, p<0.0001) and Western blot (Figure 6D)

claim: CPT-induced DSBs measured by neutral comet assay were attenuated in AtmKD/- cells
source: Moreover CPT-induced DSBs measured by phosphorylated H2AX (γ-H2AX) and the neutral comet assay were also attenuated in AtmKD/- cells (but not Atm-/- cells) and by ATM kinase inhibitor (Figure 6C–E).
evidence: Neutral comet assay results (Figure 6E, p<0.0001)

claim: CPT-induced DSBs were not attenuated in Atm-/- cells
source: Moreover CPT-induced DSBs measured by phosphorylated H2AX (γ-H2AX) and the neutral comet assay were also attenuated in AtmKD/- cells (but not Atm-/- cells) and by ATM kinase inhibitor (Figure 6C–E).
evidence: γ-H2AX and comet assay results showing normal DSB levels in Atm-/- cells (Figure 6C-E)

claim: ATM kinase inhibitor attenuated CPT-induced DSBs
source: Moreover CPT-induced DSBs measured by phosphorylated H2AX (γ-H2AX) and the neutral comet assay were also attenuated in AtmKD/- cells (but not Atm-/- cells) and by ATM kinase inhibitor (Figure 6C–E).
evidence: γ-H2AX and comet assay with ATM inhibitor (Figure 6C-E)

claim: CPT effectively increased alkaline comet tails in Atm+/-, Atm-/- and AtmKD/- cells
source: In the same cells, CPT effectively increased alkaline comet tails, an indicator of both single and double stand breaks, in Atm+/-, Atm-/- and AtmKD/- cells (Figure 6F).
evidence: Alkaline comet assay results (Figure 6F, p<0.0001 for all genotypes)

claim: Mre11 binds to ssDNA with higher affinity than to dsDNA
source: Notably, Mre11 also binds to ssDNA and the affinity of Mre11 to ssDNA is higher than to dsDNA and is independent of DNA ends (de Jager et al., 2001; Usui et al., 1998; Paull and Gellert, 1999).
evidence: Previous published findings

claim: Mre11 binding to ssDNA is independent of DNA ends
source: Notably, Mre11 also binds to ssDNA and the affinity of Mre11 to ssDNA is higher than to dsDNA and is independent of DNA ends (de Jager et al., 2001; Usui et al., 1998; Paull and Gellert, 1999).
evidence: Previous published findings

claim: MRE11 has been identified at stalled replication forks in vivo
source: Correspondingly, recent iPOND experiments have identified MRE11 at the stalled replication fork in vivo (Sirbu et al., 2011).
evidence: Previous iPOND experimental findings

claim: ATM kinase inhibitor prevents CPT induced DSBs formation in Mre11+/- but not in Mre11-/- MEFs
source: In this context, we found that ATM kinase inhibitor prevents CPT induced DSBs formation in Mre11+/- but not in Mre11-/- MEFs.
evidence: Western blot analysis of γ-H2AX in different Mre11 genotypes (Figure 7A, Figure 7—figure supplement 1A-C)

claim: The presence of nuclease deficient Mre11 is sufficient to abolish CPT induced DSBs in the presence of ATM kinase inhibitor
source: The presence of a nuclease deficient Mre11 (Mre11nuc/-) that binds and recruits ATM (Buis et al., 2008) is sufficient to abolished CPT induced DSBs in the presence of ATM kinase inhibitor (Figure 7A, Figure 7—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: Western blot analysis showing reduced γ-H2AX in Mre11nuc/- cells with ATM inhibitor (Figure 7A, Figure 7—figure supplement 1A-C)

claim: ATM kinase inhibitor did not alter the frequency of CPT induced ssDNA in Atm+/- cells
source: Moreover, we found that ATM kinase inhibitor did not alter the frequency or size of CPT induced ssDNA, or the frequency of actual fork reversal in Atm+/- cells measured by electron-microscopy (Zellweger et al., 2015)(Figure 7B and C).
evidence: Electron microscopy analysis of ssDNA at forks (Figure 7B)
